frank (devex): Heads up: release job completed but post-release checks flagged generated types changed after tagging. Noticed on sdk-node.
anya: yikes. do we have the logs?
frank (devex): paste from the action: ```
Run: yarn workspace @redwood/sdk-node typegen:check
ERROR: Generated types out of date: src/types/openapi.d.ts
Diff: - bar?: string  + bar: string
Please run: yarn typegen:regen and commit.
```
release-bot: Release created: @redwood/sdk-node v1.14.0 (tag: v1.14.0)
frank (devex): The changelog mentioned "types: stricter" so the spec change already made it into the changelog, but the tag was created before the regen commit landed.
mike (eng): Sounds like a race where changelog/run-order and typegen weren't gated. Our release workflow generates changelog, creates tag, pushes, then runs post-publish checks. If typegen changes after tag, CI will fail but the release is already published.
anya: Can we automate a pre-tag hook in the GH action that runs typegen and fails if it produces unstaged changes?
frank (devex): Proposed small guard in release action: run `yarn typegen:check` and if it returns non-zero, fail before creating tag. Also pin typegen CLI to 2.0.3 in the action container to avoid different machine behavior.
mike (eng): I also recommend adding a dedicated step: run typegen, and if it modifies files, create a commit with message `chore(gen): regen types` and abort the action so human can review. Auto-committing in release action is risky.
typegen-bot: Typegen service: current CLI version 2.1.0 detected on runners. Note: 2.1.0 changed default optional-flag handling.
frank (devex): Good call. We'll pin to 2.0.3 until we intentionally adopt 2.1.0 and audit impacts.
anya: For immediate remediation: do we revert the tag and republish or publish a patch?
mike (eng): Practical route: push a regen commit to main with the updated types, then cut v1.14.1 patch that references v1.14.0 changelog and marks it as post-release fix. Simpler than unpublishing.
frank (devex): I'll prepare the regen commit and open a PR. Also opening a follow-up to modify .github/workflows/release.yml with this snippet: ```yaml
- name: Check generated types
  run: |
    yarn workspace @redwood/sdk-node typegen:check || (echo "Typegen diffs found; please run `yarn typegen:regen` and commit. Failing release." && exit 1)
  shell: bash
```
ci-bot: [CI] PR #1001: typecheck [32mOK[0m, unit tests OK, typegen-check failed (expected diff present in branch)
anya: CI failing on the regen PR is good — means the check will block accidental mergers without an explicit regen commit.
frank (devex): After #1001 merges I'll cut the v1.14.1 patch and update the release playbook. I'll also add a docs note about ordering: openapi change -> regen types -> commit -> generate changelog -> tag.
mike (eng): Long-term: add a lint rule in CI that rejects PRs that change generated files unless commit title contains `chore(gen):` and includes a PR link to a regen commit. Could be enforced by a small script.
frank (devex): Agreed. Filing an issue to track automation + pinning: https://github.com/redwood-inference/dev-ex/issues/452
anya: Thanks frank. Please @mention the releases oncall when you cut the patch so we can coordinate marketplace updates.
frank (devex): Will do. Merging regen PR now when green and then bumping.

-- end thread --
